2609.05227.title: CABAL: Multi-Agent Simulacra for Tracing the Effects of Collusive Bidding in Peer Review
2609.05227.paper_summary: Recent reports during the AAAI-27 review cycle highlight the risk of reviewers coordinating bids for reciprocal assignment advantage. Prior work treats bidding, reviewer assignment, and review manipulation as separate stages, leaving the lifecycle effects of collusive bidding unclear. Real-world analysis is further constrained by typically unobservable collusive intent and the lack of counterfactuals for the same conference. Motivated by this gap, we introduce \alg, an end-to-end multi-agent simulacra framework for studying reviewer assignment integrity by holding the conference environment fixed and configuring LLM-driven reviewer agents with honest or collusive policies. We further develop an affinity-guided collusive bidding strategy that uses mutual reviewer-paper affinities to construct collusion rings and select target papers, producing expertise-consistent rather than arbitrarily targeted attacks. Controlled experiments show that collusive bidding more than doubles target-paper capture and that assigned colluders score target papers about two points higher than honest co-reviewers, while conference-wide effects remain comparatively modest. Evaluated bid-phase detectors provide only limited evidence of collusion: in a fixed-triplet detector stress test, native positive-bid graphs are confounded by benign affinity, while a Very-High-only diagnostic view enables precise but low-coverage local recovery.
2609.05227.paper_summary_zh: 最近在AAAI-27審查周期中的報告突顯了審稿人協調出價以獲得互惠分配優勢的風險。先前的研究將出價、審稿人分配和審稿操控視為獨立階段，導致共謀出價的生命周期效應不明確。現實世界的分析進一步受到通常不可觀察的共謀意圖和缺乏相同會議的反事實的限制。基於這一空白，我們引入\alg，一個端到端的多代理模擬框架，用於通過固定會議環境並配置具有誠實或共謀政策的LLM驅動審稿人代理來研究審稿人分配的完整性。我們進一步開發了一種親和力引導的共謀出價策略，利用互相的審稿人-論文親和力來構建共謀圈並選擇目標論文，產生一致專業知識的攻擊，而不是任意針對的攻擊。控制實驗顯示，共謀出價使目標論文的捕獲率增加了兩倍以上，而被分配的共謀者對目標論文的評分比誠實的共同審稿人高出約兩分，儘管會議整體效果仍然相對溫和。評估的出價階段檢測器僅提供有限的共謀證據：在固定三元組檢測器壓力測試中，本土的正出價圖受到良性親和力的混淆，而僅限於非常高的診斷視圖則能夠實現精確但覆蓋率低的局部恢復。
